Here's the complete working MCP HTTP server project in `/tmp/sv-4f01f9d26ef8440cafa4bd9e16af26dd/McpHttpServer/`:

## Key Files

**Program.cs** — Minimal setup with 3 builder calls:
```csharp
builder.Services.AddMcpServer()
    .WithHttpTransport()        // Streamable HTTP transport
    .WithToolsFromAssembly()    // Auto-discovers [McpServerToolType] classes
    .WithResourcesFromAssembly(); // Auto-discovers [McpServerResourceType] classes

app.MapMcp();  // Maps the MCP endpoint at root "/"
```

**ConfigResource.cs** — Resources use `[McpServerResourceType]` on the class and `[McpServerResource]` on methods:
- `UriTemplate` — the resource URI clients use to read it
- `Name` — human-readable identifier
- `MimeType` — content type of the response
- `[Description]` attribute on the method provides the description

**ServerTools.cs** — Tools use `[McpServerToolType]` on the class and `[McpServerTool]` on methods.

## How it works

`MapMcp()` sets up the **Streamable HTTP** transport at the root path. Clients POST JSON-RPC to `/` with `Accept: text/event-stream`. You can pass a route pattern like `app.MapMcp("/mcp")` to change the endpoint path.

The server was verified running — it responds with capabilities advertising both `resources` and `tools`.
